readings.title: The Sabbath of the Land and the Yoḇel
readings.subtitle: Proclaiming Release and Return to Possessions
readings.text: [Leviticus 25:1] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> spoke to Mosheh on Mount Sinai, saying, [2] <dq>“Speak to the children of Yisra’ěl, and say to them, ‘When you come into the land which <dn>I</dn> give you, then the land shall observe a Sabbath to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.</dq> [3] <dq>‘Six years you sow your field, and six years you prune your vineyard, and gather in its fruit,</dq> [4] <dq>but in the seventh year the land is to have a Sabbath of rest, a Sabbath to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. Do not sow your field and do not prune your vineyard.</dq> [5] <dq>‘Do not reap <dn>את</dn> what grows of its own of your harvest, and do not gather <dn>את</dn> the grapes of your unpruned vine, for it is a year of rest for the land.</dq> [6] <dq>‘And the Sabbath of the land shall be to you for food, for you and your servant, and for your female servant and your hired servant, and for the stranger who sojourns with you,</dq> [7] <dq>and for your livestock and the beasts that are in your land. All its crops are for food.</dq> [8] <dq>‘And you shall count seven Sabbaths of years for yourself, seven times seven years. And the time of the seven Sabbaths of years shall be to you forty-nine years.</dq> [9] <dq>‘You shall then sound a shophar-sound on the tenth day of the seventh new moon, on Yom haKippurim cause a shophar to sound through all your land.</dq> [10] <dq>‘And you shall set <dn>את</dn> the fiftieth year apart, and proclaim release throughout all the land to all its inhabitants, it is a Yoḇel for you. And each of you shall return to his possession, and each of you return to his clan.</dq> [11] <dq>‘The fiftieth year is a Yoḇel to you. Do not sow, nor reap <dn>את</dn> what grows of its own, nor gather from <dn>את</dn> its unpruned vine.</dq> [12] <dq>‘It is a Yoḇel, it is set-apart to you. Eat from the field <dn>את</dn> its crops.</dq> [13] <dq>‘In the Year of this Yoḇel let each one of you return to his possession.</dq> [14] <dq>‘And when you sell whatever to your neighbour or buy from the hand of your neighbour, do not exploit <dn>את</dn> one another.</dq> [15] <dq>‘According to the number of years after the Yoḇel you buy from <dn>את</dn> your neighbour, and according to the number of years of crops he sells to you.</dq> [16] <dq>‘According to the greater number of years you increase its price, and according to the fewer number of years you diminish its price, because he sells to you according to the number of the years of the crops.</dq> [17] <dq>‘And do not oppress <dn>את</dn> one another, but you shall fear your <dn>Elohim</dn>. For <dn>I</dn> am <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn>.</dq> [18] <dq>‘And you shall do <dn>את</dn> <dn>My</dn> laws and guard <dn>את</dn> <dn>My</dn> right-rulings, and shall do <dn>את</dn> them. And you shall dwell in the land in safety,</dq> [19] <dq>‘and the land shall yield its fruit, and you shall eat to satisfaction, and shall dwell there in safety.</dq> [20] <dq>‘And since you might say, “What do we eat in the seventh year, since we do not sow nor gather in <dn>את</dn> our crops?”</dq> [21] <dq>‘Therefore <dn>I</dn> have commanded <dn>את</dn> <dn>My</dn> blessing on you in the sixth year, and it shall bring forth <dn>את</dn> the crop for three years.</dq> [22] <dq>‘And you shall sow in <dn>את</dn> the eighth year, and eat of the old crop until the ninth year. Eat of the old until its crop comes in.</dq> [23] <dq>‘And the land is not to be sold beyond reclaim, for the land is <dn>Mine</dn>, for you are sojourners and settlers with <dn>Me</dn>.</dq>

readings.title: The Redemption of Property
readings.subtitle: Reclaiming the Land and Lěvitical Cities
readings.text: [Leviticus 25:24] <dq>‘And provide for a redemption for the land, in all the land of your possession.</dq> [25] <dq>‘When your brother becomes poor, and has sold some of his possession, and his redeemer, a close relative comes to redeem it, then he shall redeem <dn>את</dn> what his brother sold.</dq> [26] <dq>‘And when the man has no one to redeem it, but he himself becomes able to redeem it,</dq> [27] <dq>then let him count <dn>את</dn> the years since its sale, and return <dn>את</dn> the remainder to the man to whom he sold it, that he shall return to his possession.</dq> [28] <dq>‘And if his hand has not found enough to give back to him, then what was sold shall remain in the hand of him who bought <dn>את</dn> it until the Year of Yoḇel. And it shall be released in the Yoḇel, and he shall return to his possession.</dq> [29] <dq>‘And when a man sells a house in a walled city, then his right of redemption shall be at the end of the year after it is sold. His right of redemption lasts a year.</dq> [30] <dq>‘But if it is not redeemed within a complete year, then the house in the walled city shall be established beyond reclaim to the buyer of <dn>את</dn> it, throughout his generations. It is not released in the Yoḇel.</dq> [31] <dq>‘The houses of villages, however, which have no wall around them are reckoned as the field of the country. A right of redemption belongs to it, and they are released in the Yoḇel.</dq> [32] <dq>‘As for the cities of the Lěvites, and the houses in the cities of their possession, the Lěvites have a right of redemption forever.</dq> [33] <dq>‘And that which is redeemed from the Lěvites, both the sale of a house and the city of his possession shall be released in the Year of Yoḇel, because the houses in the cities of the Lěvites are their possession in the midst of the children of Yisra’ěl.</dq> [34] <dq>‘But the field of the open land of their cities is not sold, for it is their everlasting possession.</dq>

readings.title: The Redemption of the Poor
readings.subtitle: The Prohibition of Harsh Rule and Usury
readings.text: [Leviticus 25:35] <dq>‘And when your brother becomes poor, and his hand has failed with you, then you shall strengthen him, and he shall live with you, like a stranger or a sojourner.</dq> [36] <dq>‘Take no interest from <dn>את</dn> him, or profit, but you shall fear your <dn>Elohim</dn>, and your brother shall live with you.</dq> [37] <dq>‘Do not lend him <dn>את</dn> your silver on interest, and do not lend him your food for profit.</dq> [38] <dq>‘<dn>I</dn> am <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn>, who brought <dn>את</dn> you out of the land of Mitsrayim, to give you <dn>את</dn> the land of Kena‛an, to be your <dn>Elohim</dn>.</dq> [39] <dq>‘And when your brother who dwells by you becomes poor, and sells himself to you, do not make him serve as a slave.</dq> [40] <dq>‘But as a hired servant, as a settler he is with you, and serves you until the Year of Yoḇel.</dq> [41] <dq>‘And then he shall leave you, he and his children with him, and shall return to his own clan, even return to the possession of his fathers.</dq> [42] <dq>‘For they are <dn>My</dn> servants, whom <dn>I</dn> brought <dn>את</dn> out of the land of Mitsrayim, they are not sold as slaves.</dq> [43] <dq>‘Do not rule over him with harshness, but you shall fear your <dn>Elohim</dn>.</dq> [44] <dq>‘And your male and female slaves whom you have from <dn>את</dn> the nations that are around you, from them you buy male and female slaves,</dq> [45] <dq>and also from the sons of the strangers sojourning among you, from them you buy, and from their clans who are with you, which they shall bring forth in your land, and they shall be your property.</dq> [46] <dq>‘And you shall take <dn>את</dn> them as an inheritance for your children after you, to inherit them as a possession, they are your slaves for all time. But over your brothers, the children of Yisra’ěl, you do not rule with harshness, one over another.</dq> [47] <dq>‘Now when a sojourner or a settler with you becomes rich, and your brother with him becomes poor, and sells himself to the settler or sojourner with you, or to a member of the sojourner’s clan,</dq> [48] <dq>after he has been sold, there is a right of redemption to him – one of his brothers does redeem him,</dq> [49] <dq>or his uncle or his uncle’s son does redeem him, or anyone who is a close relative to him in his clan does redeem him, or if he is able, then he shall redeem himself.</dq> [50] <dq>‘And he shall reckon with him who bought him: The price of his release shall be according to the number of years, from the year that he was sold to him until the Year of Yoḇel; as the days of a hired servant it is with him.</dq> [51] <dq>‘If there are yet many years, according to them he repays the price of his redemption, from the silver of his purchase.</dq> [52] <dq>‘And if few years are left until the Year of Yoḇel, then he shall reckon with him, and according to his years he repays him <dn>את</dn> the price of his redemption.</dq> [53] <dq>‘He is with him as a yearly hired servant, and he does not rule with harshness over him before your eyes.</dq> [54] <dq>‘And if he is not redeemed in these years, then he shall be released in the Year of Yoḇel, he and his children with him.</dq> [55] <dq>‘Because the children of Yisra’ěl are servants to <dn>Me</dn>, they are <dn>My</dn> servants whom <dn>I</dn> brought <dn>את</dn> out of the land of Mitsrayim. <dn>I</dn> am <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn>.</dq>

readings.title: The Blessings of Emunah
readings.subtitle: Fruitfulness, Peace, and the Divine Dwelling
readings.text: [Leviticus 26:1] <dq>‘Do not make idols for yourselves, and do not set up a carved image or a pillar for yourselves, and do not place a stone image in your land, to bow down to it. For <dn>I</dn> am <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn>.</dq> [2] <dq>‘Guard <dn>את</dn> <dn>My</dn> Sabbaths and reverence <dn>My</dn> set-apart place. <dn>I</dn> am <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.</dq> [3] <dq>‘If you walk in <dn>My</dn> laws and guard <dn>את</dn> <dn>My</dn> commands, and shall do <dn>את</dn> them,</dq> [4] <dq>then <dn>I</dn> shall give you rain in its season, and the land shall yield its crops, and the trees of the field yield their fruit.</dq> [5] <dq>‘And your threshing shall last till <dn>את</dn> the time of the grape harvest, and the grape harvest shall last till <dn>את</dn> the time of sowing. And you shall eat your bread until you have enough, and shall dwell in your land safely.</dq> [6] <dq>‘And <dn>I</dn> shall give peace in the land, and you shall lie down and no one make you afraid. And <dn>I</dn> shall clear the land of evil beasts, and not let the sword go through your land.</dq> [7] <dq>‘And you shall pursue <dn>את</dn> your enemies, and they shall fall by the sword before you.</dq> [8] <dq>‘And five of you shall pursue a hundred, and a hundred of you pursue ten thousand. And your enemies shall fall by the sword before you.</dq> [9] <dq>‘And <dn>I</dn> shall turn to you and make <dn>את</dn> you fruitful, and shall increase <dn>את</dn> you, and shall establish <dn>את</dn> <dn>My</dn> covenant with <dn>את</dn> you.</dq> [10] <dq>‘And you shall eat the old supply, and clear out the old because of the new.</dq> [11] <dq>‘And <dn>I</dn> shall set <dn>My</dn> Dwelling Place in your midst, and <dn>My</dn> being shall not reject <dn>את</dn> you.</dq> [12] <dq>‘And <dn>I</dn> shall walk in your midst, and shall be your <dn>Elohim</dn>, and you shall be <dn>My</dn> people.</dq> [13] <dq>‘<dn>I</dn> am <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn>, who brought <dn>את</dn> you out of the land of Mitsrayim, from being their slaves. And <dn>I</dn> have broken the bars of your yoke and made <dn>את</dn> you walk upright.</dq>

readings.title: The Consequences of Anomia
readings.subtitle: The Sevenfold Punishments and the Promise of Remembrance
readings.text: [Leviticus 26:14] <dq>‘But if you do not obey <dn>Me</dn>, and do not do <dn>את</dn> all these commands,</dq> [15] <dq>and if you reject <dn>My</dn> laws, or if your being loathes <dn>את</dn> <dn>My</dn> right-rulings, so that you do not do <dn>את</dn> all <dn>My</dn> commands, but break <dn>את</dn> <dn>My</dn> covenant,</dq> [16] <dq><dn>I</dn> also do this to you: And <dn>I</dn> shall appoint sudden alarm over you, <dn>את</dn> wasting disease and <dn>את</dn> inflammation, destroying the eyes, and consuming the life. And you shall sow your seed in vain, for your enemies shall eat it.</dq> [17] <dq>‘And <dn>I</dn> shall set <dn>My</dn> face against you, and you shall be smitten before your enemies. And those who hate you shall rule over you, and you shall flee when no one pursues <dn>את</dn> you.</dq> [18] <dq>‘And after all this, if you do not obey <dn>Me</dn>, then <dn>I</dn> shall punish <dn>את</dn> you seven times more for your sins.</dq> [19] <dq>‘And <dn>I</dn> shall break <dn>את</dn> the pride of your power, and shall make <dn>את</dn> your heavens like iron and <dn>את</dn> your earth like bronze.</dq> [20] <dq>‘And your strength shall be spent in vain and your land not yield <dn>את</dn> its crops, nor the trees of the land yield their fruit.</dq> [21] <dq>‘And if you walk contrary to <dn>Me</dn>, and refuse to obey <dn>Me</dn>, <dn>I</dn> shall bring on you seven times more plagues, according to your sins,</dq> [22] <dq>and send <dn>את</dn> wild beasts among you, which shall bereave <dn>את</dn> you of your children. And <dn>I</dn> shall cut off <dn>את</dn> your livestock, and make <dn>את</dn> you few in number, and your highways shall be deserted.</dq> [23] <dq>‘And if you are not instructed by <dn>Me</dn> by these, but walk contrary to <dn>Me</dn>,</dq> [24] <dq>then <dn>I</dn> also shall walk contrary to you, and <dn>I</dn> <dn>Myself</dn> shall strike <dn>את</dn> you seven times for your sins.</dq> [25] <dq>‘And <dn>I</dn> shall bring against you a sword executing the vengeance of <dn>My</dn> covenant, and you shall gather together in your cities, and <dn>I</dn> shall send pestilence among you, and you shall be given into the hand of the enemy.</dq> [26] <dq>‘When <dn>I</dn> have cut off your supply of bread, ten women shall bake your bread in one oven, and they shall bring back to you your bread by weight, and you shall eat and not be satisfied.</dq> [27] <dq>‘And if in spite of this, you do not obey <dn>Me</dn>, but walk contrary to <dn>Me</dn>,</dq> [28] <dq>then <dn>I</dn> shall walk contrary to you in wrath. And <dn>I</dn> <dn>Myself</dn> shall punish <dn>את</dn> you seven times for your sins.</dq> [29] <dq>‘And you shall eat the flesh of your sons, and eat the flesh of your daughters.</dq> [30] <dq>‘And <dn>I</dn> shall destroy <dn>את</dn> your high places, and cut down <dn>את</dn> your sun-pillars, and put <dn>את</dn> your carcasses on the carcasses of your idols. And <dn>My</dn> being shall loathe <dn>את</dn> you.</dq> [31] <dq>‘And <dn>I</dn> shall turn <dn>את</dn> your cities into ruins and lay <dn>את</dn> your set-apart places waste, and not smell your sweet fragrances.</dq> [32] <dq>‘And <dn>I</dn> shall lay <dn>את</dn> the land waste, and your enemies who dwell in it shall be astonished at it.</dq> [33] <dq>‘And <dn>I</dn> shall scatter <dn>את</dn> you among the nations and draw out a sword after you. And your land shall be desert and your cities ruins,</dq> [34] <dq>and the land enjoy <dn>את</dn> its Sabbaths as long as it lies waste and you are in your enemies’ land. Then the land would rest and enjoy <dn>את</dn> its Sabbaths.</dq> [35] <dq>‘As long as it lies waste it rests, for the time <dn>את</dn> it did not rest on your Sabbaths when you dwelt in it.</dq> [36] <dq>‘And as for those of you who are left, <dn>I</dn> shall send faintness into their hearts in the lands of their enemies, and the sound of a shaken leaf shall cause <dn>את</dn> them to flee. And they shall flee as though retreating from a sword, and they shall fall when no one pursues.</dq> [37] <dq>‘And they shall stumble over one another, as from before a sword, when no one pursues. And you shall be unable to stand before your enemies.</dq> [38] <dq>‘And you shall perish among the nations, and the land of your enemies shall eat <dn>את</dn> you up,</dq> [39] <dq>and those of you who are left rot away in their crookedness in your enemies’ lands, and also in their fathers’ crookednesses rot away with them.</dq> [40] <dq>‘But if they confess <dn>את</dn> their crookedness and <dn>את</dn> the crookedness of their fathers, with their trespass in which they trespassed against <dn>Me</dn>, and that they also have walked contrary to <dn>Me</dn>,</dq> [41] <dq>and that <dn>I</dn> also have walked contrary to them and have brought <dn>את</dn> them into the land of their enemies – if their uncircumcised heart is then humbled, and they accept <dn>את</dn> the punishment of their crookedness,</dq> [42] <dq>then <dn>I</dn> shall remember <dn>את</dn> <dn>My</dn> covenant with Ya‛aqoḇ, and also <dn>את</dn> <dn>My</dn> covenant with Yitsḥaq, and also remember <dn>את</dn> <dn>My</dn> covenant with Aḇraham, and remember the land.</dq> [43] <dq>‘For the land was abandoned by them, and enjoying <dn>את</dn> its Sabbaths while lying waste without them, and they were paying for <dn>את</dn> their crookedness, because they rejected <dn>My</dn> right-rulings and because their being loathed <dn>את</dn> <dn>My</dn> laws.</dq> [44] <dq>‘And yet for all this, when they are in the land of their enemies, <dn>I</dn> shall not reject them, nor shall <dn>I</dn> loathe them so as to destroy them and break <dn>My</dn> covenant with them. For <dn>I</dn> am <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> their <dn>Elohim</dn>.</dq> [45] <dq>‘Then <dn>I</dn> shall remember for their sake the covenant of the ancestors whom <dn>I</dn> brought <dn>את</dn> out of the land of Mitsrayim before the eyes of the nations to be their <dn>Elohim</dn>. <dn>I</dn> am <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.’ ”</dq> [46] These are the laws and the right-rulings and the Torot which <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> made between <dn>Himself</dn> and the children of Yisra’ěl on Mount Sinai by the hand of Mosheh.
